To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the organoleptic quality of tomato fruit is a complex trait that depends on numerous factors and that is difficult to measure; (2) we identified a number of traits contributing to fruit quality and to sensory attributes; (3) the genetic background of tomato ecotypes is more relevant to the organoleptic traits related to texture, while the environmental conditions are more relevant to those related to flavour perception.
we identified a number of biochemical and sensory traits contributing to tomato organoleptic properties.

1) the sensory attributes of sweetness, sourness and tomato flavour are more influenced by the environmental conditions, 2) the attributes of juiciness, hardness, granulosity and equatorial diameter are more influenced by genetic constitution of the cultivar, and 3) the sensory attributes related to taste perception are more influenced by agronomic factors, while those related to texture are more influenced by environmental factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the most important sensory attributes that contribute to tomato organoleptic characteristics.
the identification of the most suitable selection criteria to be used for the improvement of organoleptic quality in tomato.
the genetic and agronomic factors involved in the sensory quality of tomato fruit and their relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensory attributes of tomato are not influenced by environmental conditions, but rather by the genotype of the ecotype.
the sensory quality of tomato fruit is influenced by the genetic and environmental conditions, with a greater impact of the latter.
the genetic background of tomato cultivars is more relevant than the environmental conditions in determining the perception of sensory quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sensory attributes related to taste perception are mainly influenced by environmental conditions, while those linked to texture and colour are mainly influenced by the genetic background of tomato.
sensory quality of tomato fruit is the result of both the genetic constitution of the cultivar and the environmental conditions in which the plant grows.

the sensory perception of tomato flavour is more closely related to agronomic traits, whereas the sensory attributes linked to texture perception are more related to the genetic constitution and the biochemical content of tomato.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sensory traits are not only influenced by environmental conditions but also by the genetic background of cultivars.
the sensory attributes of tomatoes are not only affected by the genetic constitution of the cultivar, but also by the environment in which it is grown.

, in order to improve sensory quality, it is necessary to take into account the environmental conditions in which tomato is grown and to consider that some sensory attributes are more sensitive to environmental conditions than to the genetic background.
